H2: Motion artifacts in accelerometer channel cause heteroscedastic noise.

Variables: accelerometer variance (e.g., RMS of high-frequency components), residual variance, prediction interval width, coverage.

Causal path: More motion artifact -> higher local variance -> nonconformity scores assume homoscedastic -> quantile underestimates needed width for high-variance periods -> intervals too narrow -> undercoverage.

Expected direction: Increase in motion artifact variance leads to decrease in coverage.

Boundary conditions: periods of movement (e.g., when subject is walking or performing tasks), sampling rate, sensor placement.

Outcomes: coverage, interval width, Breusch-Pagan test for heteroscedasticity.

Notes: need to label motion artifact via accelerometer magnitude > threshold.

H3: Temporal non-stationarity (habituation). Variables: time since start, stress label probability, residual mean shift, coverage.

Causal path: As time progresses, habituation reduces physiological response -> true stress label distribution shifts -> calibration based on early data misrepresents later -> conformity scores biased -> intervals too narrow -> undercoverage for later segments.

Expected direction: Later time -> lower coverage.

Boundary conditions: stress episodes occurring after adaptation period (>10 min), baseline stable.

Outcomes: coverage per time bin, Kolmogorov-Smirnov test between early and late residuals, interval width.

Notes: need to split data into early vs late.

H4: Misaligned timestamps between ECG and respiration.

Variables: timestamp offset (ms), cross-correlation coefficient between ECG-derived features and respiration features, residual mean, coverage.

Causal path: Misalignment -> spurious correlation -> model overconfident -> residuals shrunk -> intervals narrow -> undercoverage.

Expected direction: Larger offset -> lower coverage.

Boundary conditions: ECG and respiration sampled at same nominal rate but unknown offset; need to consider periods where both signals present.

Outcomes: coverage, interval width, cross-correlation lag analysis.

Notes: need to estimate offset via maximizing mutual information.

H5: Labeling inconsistencies.

Variables: label noise level (e.g., inter-annotator disagreement, entropy), conformity score distribution, coverage.

Causal path: Noisy labels -> observed conformity scores inflated (since model penalized for mismatched labels) -> quantile underestimates true uncertainty -> intervals narrow -> undercoverage.

Expected direction: Higher label noise -> lower coverage.

Boundary conditions: periods where annotators disagree, ambiguous stress cues.

Outcomes: coverage, interval width, label entropy, Cohen's kappa between annotators.

Notes: need to obtain multiple annotator labels or use confidence scores.

H6: Stratification by stress intensity ignores subject-specific baseline shifts.

Variables: subject baseline arousal (e.g., mean skin conductance level), stratum (low/medium/high stress), residual mean per stratum, coverage.

Causal path: Using global strata fails to adjust for individual offset -> residuals for low-baseline subjects systematically shifted -> conformity scores biased -> intervals narrow -> undercoverage for those subjects.

Expected direction: Lower baseline arousal -> lower coverage (if stratification too high).

Boundary conditions: stress intensity levels defined by predefined thresholds (e.g., based on self-report), baseline measured during rest.

Outcomes: coverage per subject baseline group, interval width, bias of residuals (mean).

Notes: need to compute baseline per subject.

H7: Small calibration set size.

Variables: number of calibration samples per subject, standard error of quantile estimate, interval width, coverage.

Causal path: Fewer calibration samples -> higher sampling error of empirical quantile -> estimated quantile too low (optimistic) -> intervals narrower -> undercoverage.

Expected direction: Smaller calibration size -> lower coverage.

Boundary conditions: calibration set drawn from stress episodes only; need at least N_min.

Outcomes: coverage, interval width, quantile confidence interval width.

Notes: can simulate via bootstrap.

H8: Non-linear interactions between GSR and temperature not captured by linear scoring function.

Variables: GSR, temperature, interaction term (product), residual from linear model, nonconformity score, coverage.

Causal path: Missing interaction -> model mis-specifies relationship -> residuals larger for subjects with strong coupling but not captured -> conformity scores miscalibrated -> intervals narrow -> undercoverage.

Expected direction: Stronger GSR-temperature interaction (higher product) -> lower coverage.

Boundary conditions: periods where both GSR and temperature vary (e.g., during stress), sensor placement.

Outcomes: coverage, interval width, test for non-linearity (e.g., Ramsey RESET), interaction significance.

Notes: need to fit linear vs non-linear model.

H9: Medication/caffeine intake altering physiological dynamics.

Variables: caffeine dosage (mg), medication presence (binary), physiological response parameters (e.g., HRV, GSR slope), residual distribution, coverage.

Causal path: Substance -> altered baseline and responsiveness -> different error characteristics -> exchangeability violated across cohort -> intervals miscalibrated -> undercoverage for affected subjects.

Expected direction: Presence of caffeine/medication -> lower coverage.

Boundary conditions: subjects self-report intake within 2h before recording; control for dosage.

Outcomes: coverage per substance group, interval width, Kolmogorov-Smirnov test between groups.

Notes: need to log intake.

H10: Window-based feature extraction edge effects uneven across subjects.

Variables: window length (s), stress bout duration, feature bias (difference between true and windowed feature), residual mean, coverage.

Causal path: Short stress bouts -> window includes pre/post non-stress data -> feature values diluted -> model predicts less extreme -> conformity scores inflated -> intervals narrow -> undercoverage for short bouts.

Expected direction: Shorter bout length relative to window -> lower coverage.

Boundary conditions: stress bouts defined by annotation; window length fixed (e.g., 10s); need bouts < window length.

Outcomes: coverage for short vs long bouts, interval width, feature bias measurement.

Notes: need to compute features with varying window lengths to test.
